coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Community Center Garage (UCSF Mission Bay)
record.summary: UCSF lists a 'Community Center Garage' at 1625 Owens Street among its Mission Bay campus parking options, and DataSF's official address point for 1625 Owens St lies inside this record's outline. No source read says when, by whom or how it was built; the May 2000 Regents item for the neighbouring community center says an interim parking lot would be built beside it 'until a parking structure can be built in a later phase'.

notes.accuracy_caveat: PARTIALLY REAL -- UCSF's June 2025 CAC map (updated December 2024) labels this 'COMMUNITY CENTER GARAGE (21A)' with a parking symbol and does not list it among the undeveloped parcels, which supports an existing garage here; the rooftop deck and painted parking-space striping are Pier & Point's own reading of satellite imagery (not cited or saved here), and this record's own boundary was traced as the leftover open ground between DataSF's official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes, as seen in satellite imagery, not a surveyed building footprint or parcel line; DataSF's Building Footprints dataset (the copy held in this project's data, loaded October 2026) does not separate this garage from the Rutter Center building: one footprint of about 8,100 sq m (map-block-lot reference SF8709011) covers the Rutter Center and about 40 percent of the area drawn here, so there is no official boundary between 21A and 21B -- the dividing line used here is the Rutter Center's own real west wall, extended, which is a reasonable but not authoritative choice.
notes.digitized_from: Traced as the leftover open ground between DataSF's official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes in the Owens St / Rutter Center area, as seen in satellite imagery; several pieces were chosen and combined by hand, not taken from a surveyed parcel. changes.text: Long 'At a glance' values were cut to the fact itself (or 'Sources differ'); the disputes, quoted excerpts and hedging moved to this record's open questions, with every source still named. No change to the record's status or shape.

The Community Center Garage page now cites UCSF's Brain Tumor Center parking page, which lists a Community Center Garage at 1625 Owens St, as the source of the address. It also says what DataSF's building-footprint data shows: one footprint runs across the Rutter Center and about 40 percent of the area drawn here, so the data has no boundary between the two. The painted stalls and the rooftop deck remain Pier & Point's own reading of satellite imagery.
The page now notes that a 2021 city permit record lists an existing 8-story public parking garage at 1625 Owens Street. Who built it, and when, is still not known.
Added a sourced dossier for Community Center Garage.

The garage record said a real rooftop deck with painted striping was visible in satellite imagery, that it stood beside the William J. Rutter Community Center and was joined by a walkway, and that the area was the 1625 Owens St parking lot. UCSF's June 2025 CAC map supports only an existing garage labeled 'Community Center Garage (21A)' beside 'Rutter Center (21B)'. The record now says so, marks the rooftop deck, walkway and striping as Pier & Point's own satellite reading (not cited), drops the full Rutter Center name, and flags that the 1625 Owens St address is unsourced.

open_questions: When was the Community Center Garage built, and is it a multi-level structure? UCSF's parking page (undated) offers parking at 1625 Owens St, and the city's address point is inside the outline, but no source read dates its construction or opening. A 2021 DBI permit record on the lot lists an existing public parking garage of 8 stories (see below).

STRUCTURE QUESTION: the May 2000 Regents item describes an interim parking lot beside the community center, to be replaced by a parking structure in a later phase. In UCSF's June 12, 2025 Mission Bay CAC figure (an image) the label 'COMMUNITY CENTER GARAGE (21A)' sits beside a flat, building-less parcel with a parking symbol, where it was viewed by eye, not as text. The map label alone does not settle whether a structure stands there. DBI permit 202111081961 (filed 2021-11-08, 1625 Owens St, block 8709 lot 011) records "existing_use": "prkng garage/public" and "number_of_existing_stories": "8", which indicates a multi-story public parking garage, but its description is of telecommunications equipment, not of the garage, and no source read gives a construction date. The geometry file's rooftop-deck reading comes from the project's own satellite review and is not corroborated by a document.

The Assessor's 2022 roll has one parcel (8709011, listed '1675 1625 OWENS') for the community center and the garage together, with no year built; a DBI permit search on block 8709 lot 011 returned two permits: a 2019 street-space permit (M1170767) and permit 202111081961 (filed 2021-11-08), an alteration to an existing T-Mobile telecommunications facility whose record lists the existing use as "prkng garage/public" with 8 existing stories. Neither is a new-construction permit for a garage, so no construction permit or date was found.
Architect, builder, space count and operator are not found. UCSF's Parking and Transportation pages were not opened (blocked).
The garage is distinct from the 1670 Owens garage (DBI permit 200801243180, 823 spaces), which has its own record.
No UC Regents capital item for a community-center garage was located.

record.notes: A parking garage labeled 'COMMUNITY CENTER GARAGE (21A)' on UCSF's own Dec 2024-updated campus map (June 2025 CAC presentation, page 3), immediately west of the block that map labels 'RUTTER CENTER (21B)'. UCSF's Brain Tumor Center parking page (undated) lists a 'Community Center Garage' at 1625 Owens St, which is the source of the address. That it has a rooftop deck and is connected to the Rutter Center by a walkway is Pier & Point's own reading of satellite imagery, not stated on UCSF's map, and the building's full name and operator are not confirmed by a primary source.
